name: forge-local-agent
description: A Cursor-style agentic coding assistant that runs entirely on local Ollama models. Agent/Ask/Plan modes, multitask chat tabs, .forge/rules + .forge/skills + .forge/hooks, repo-stored chat history, multi-file agent edits, inline Cmd+K editing, Tab autocomplete, and an opt-in production-grade web search/fetch tool — no cloud, no API keys, no telemetry, except web search itself if you turn it on.

commands.title: Forge: Set Model for Mode (per-mode routing)
Forge: Add File to Chat Context
Forge: Set Web Search API Key

forge.ollamaBaseUrl.description: Base URL of your local Ollama server.

forge.chatModel.description: Ollama model tag to use for chat/agent (e.g. 'qwen2.5-coder:14b'). Leave empty to auto-pick the best available coding model on first use.

forge.completionModel.description: Ollama model tag to use for Tab autocomplete (a fast, small model recommended). Leave empty to reuse the chat model.

forge.embeddingModel.description: Ollama embedding model used to index the workspace for @codebase search. If not installed, Forge falls back to keyword search automatically.

forge.maxAgentIterations.description: Maximum tool-call steps per turn in Agent/Ask/Plan mode before Forge stops and asks you to continue. The loop detector (always on) is the real safety net against thrashing now, so this just bounds a single very long turn — raise it if you hit it on legitimately long tasks.

forge.autoModeMaxIterations.description: Maximum tool-call steps per turn in Auto mode — effectively unbounded, since Auto mode is meant to run hands-off until done. The loop detector still stops it if it starts thrashing.

forge.numCtx.description: Context window size requested from Ollama (options.num_ctx) for chat/agent and inline-edit calls. Ollama's own default is small and silent about truncating — a long agent session can quietly lose early context without this set. Check your model's real max with `ollama show <model>` and set this close to it if you have the memory/VRAM to spare (the KV cache is sized to this ceiling whether or not you use all of it).

forge.modelRouting.description: Optional per-mode model overrides, e.g. {"plan": "deepseek-r1:14b", "agent": "qwen2.5-coder:14b"}. A mode with no entry here falls back to forge.chatModel. Also settable via "Forge: Set Model for Mode" (quick pick, no JSON editing needed). A chat tab's own model override (the model-name button in the composer) still wins over this.

forge.keepAliveMinutes.description: Minutes Ollama keeps a model loaded in memory after a request. -1 = never unload between messages (avoids a full reload + KV-cache rebuild every time you pause to think — set via Ollama's per-request keep_alive, which works regardless of how the Ollama server itself was launched). 0 = Ollama's own default (~5 min idle unload).

forge.requireApprovalForWrites.description: Require you to accept/reject each file edit the agent proposes before it is written to disk.

forge.requireApprovalForCommands.description: Require approval before the agent runs a terminal command, unless it matches an auto-approve pattern.

forge.autoApproveCommands.description: Regex patterns for read-only/safe commands the agent may run without asking for approval each time.

forge.enableTabCompletion.description: Enable ghost-text Tab autocomplete powered by your local model.

forge.completionDebounceMs.description: Milliseconds to wait after typing stops before requesting an autocomplete suggestion.

forge.contextChunkCount.description: Number of workspace chunks to retrieve for @codebase context.

forge.maxContextFileKB.description: Skip indexing/reading files larger than this size (KB) to keep context tight.

forge.subAgentModel.description: Ollama model tag used for spawn_subagent turns (the 'ability to spawn sub agents' feature). Leave empty to reuse whichever model the spawning turn itself is using — a good default is a smaller/faster model here, since sub-agents run tightly-scoped tasks.

forge.subAgentMaxIterations.description: Tool-call step cap for a single spawn_subagent turn — its own, tighter budget than forge.autoModeMaxIterations so a delegated sub-task can't silently run forever.

forge.maxSubAgentDepth.description: Maximum spawn_subagent nesting depth (a sub-agent spawning its own sub-agent, etc.). Clamped to a small hard ceiling regardless of this value as a safety backstop.

forge.showStatusMessages.description: Show a brief, live activity line (e.g. "Reading src/foo.ts…", "Thinking with qwen2.5-coder:14b…") in the composer footer while the agent is working.

forge.webSearch.enabled.description: Enable the web_search / web_fetch tools. OFF BY DEFAULT: this is the one Forge feature that inherently sends data outside your machine (a search query has to reach a provider; fetched pages come from third-party servers) — everything else in Forge stays fully local. Turn this on deliberately, and configure a provider API key with "Forge: Set Web Search API Key" for real search quality (the built-in DuckDuckGo fallback works with no setup but is an HTML scrape of a page not meant for programmatic use, and is more fragile / lower quality than a real search API).

forge.webSearch.provider.description: Which web search backend to use. "auto" tries every provider you've configured credentials for, in quality order (Tavily, Brave, Google, SearXNG), falling back to the no-key DuckDuckGo scrape if none are configured. Pick a specific one to pin it.

forge.webSearch.maxResults.description: Maximum results per web_search call (capped at 20 regardless of this value).

forge.webSearch.timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds for both search-provider requests and web_fetch page downloads.

forge.webSearch.cacheTtlMinutes.description: How long search results and fetched pages are cached in memory before a repeat query/URL hits the network again — avoids hammering a provider (or burning paid-API quota) if the agent searches something similar more than once in a session.

forge.webSearch.blockedDomains.description: Domains (and their subdomains) to silently drop from web_search results, e.g. ["pinterest.com"].

forge.webSearch.respectRobotsTxt.description: Whether web_fetch checks the target site's robots.txt before downloading a page and honors Disallow rules. Recommended to leave on; a missing/unreachable robots.txt is always treated as "everything allowed", never as blocking.

forge.webSearch.maxFetchChars.description: Approximate cap on how much raw page content web_fetch downloads/reads before extraction, to bound memory/time on an unexpectedly huge page.

forge.webSearch.searxngUrl.description: Base URL of a self-hosted SearXNG instance (e.g. "https://searx.example.com"), used when forge.webSearch.provider is "searxng" or as part of the "auto" fallback chain. Not a secret — stored as a plain setting, unlike API keys (see "Forge: Set Web Search API Key").
